title: 贼退示官吏
title_en: To the Officials, After the Rebels Withdrew
author: 元结

text_note.zh: 原始文本把“日晏”的“晏”放在方括号里，又有“陷隣境”“徴敛”两处繁简转换的错字，这里按通行本作“日晏”“邻境”“征敛”。通行本诗前还有一段小序：“癸卯岁，西原贼入道州，焚烧杀掠，几尽而去。明年，贼又攻永州，破邵，不犯此州边鄙而退。岂力能制敌欤？盖蒙其伤怜而已。诸使何为忍苦征敛！故作诗一篇以示官吏。”
text_note.en: The corpus puts the character yàn of rì yàn in square brackets, and has two slips from machine conversion in lín jìng (neighbouring lands) and zhēng liǎn (collecting taxes). They are corrected here to the usual text. The usual text also prints a short preface before the poem: "In the year guimao, rebels from Xiyuan broke into Daozhou. They burned, killed and robbed until almost nothing was left, then went away. The next year they attacked Yongzhou and took Shaozhou, but they did not touch the edges of this prefecture before pulling back. Was it because we were strong enough to stop them? No, it was only because they pitied us. So how can the imperial envoys bear to squeeze taxes out of these people so harshly? That is why I wrote this poem to show the officials."

readings.zh: 数岁：几年。这里的“数”读 shù，意思是“几个”，不读 shǔ。
readings.en: shù suì means several years. Here the character is read shù (a few), not shǔ (to count).

glosses.zh: 昔岁：从前的年月。
glosses.en: xī suì: years gone by, the old days.

glosses.zh: 逢太平：遇上天下太平的时候。
glosses.en: féng tài píng: to live in a time of peace.

glosses.zh: 山林二十年：在山林里住了很多年。“二十年”是大概的说法。
glosses.en: shān lín èr shí nián: lived in the hills and woods for many years. "Twenty years" is a round number.

glosses.zh: 庭户：院子和房门。
glosses.en: tíng hù: the courtyard and the door of the house.

glosses.zh: 洞壑：山洞和山谷。
glosses.en: dòng hè: caves and valleys.

glosses.zh: 当：正对着。
glosses.en: dāng: right in front of, facing.

glosses.zh: 井税：田税。古时候有把田地分成“井”字形的说法，所以田税也叫井税。
glosses.en: jǐng shuì: land tax. In old times farmland was said to be divided like the character for a well, so land tax was called "well tax".

glosses.zh: 有常期：交税有固定的日子，不会乱收。
glosses.en: yǒu cháng qī: taxes were collected on fixed dates, not at random.

glosses.zh: 日晏：太阳已经很高了，天色已晚。这句是说可以安心睡到很晚。
glosses.en: rì yàn: the sun is high, it is late in the day. The line means people could sleep in without worry.

glosses.zh: 世变：世道大变，指安史之乱。
glosses.en: shì biàn: the world turned upside down. This means the An Lushan Rebellion, a huge civil war that began in 755.

glosses.zh: 亲戎旃：亲自待在军营里，就是从军打仗。戎旃，军中的帐篷和旗子。
glosses.en: qīn róng zhān: to serve in the army in person. Róng zhān are army tents and flags.

glosses.zh: 典斯郡：掌管这个州郡。典，主管；斯，这。指元结做道州刺史（一州的长官）。
glosses.en: diǎn sī jùn: to govern this prefecture. Diǎn means to be in charge; sī means this. Yuan Jie had become governor of Daozhou.

glosses.zh: 山夷：住在山里的少数民族，这里指“西原贼”，从西原一带起兵作乱的人。
glosses.en: shān yí: hill peoples. Here it means the rebels from the Xiyuan area in the far south.

glosses.zh: 纷然：乱纷纷的样子，指又闹起事来。
glosses.en: fēn rán: in turmoil, stirring up trouble again.

glosses.zh: 屠：大批地杀人。
glosses.en: tú: to kill large numbers of people, to massacre.

glosses.zh: 伤可怜：叫人哀伤、同情。这句是说：连贼都可怜这里的百姓太穷。
glosses.en: shāng kě lián: sad and pitiful. The line means even the rebels pitied the people here for being so poor.

glosses.zh: 是以：因此。
glosses.en: shì yǐ: because of this, therefore.

glosses.zh: 陷邻境：攻破了邻近的地方。陷，攻破。
glosses.en: xiàn lín jìng: broke into the neighbouring lands. Xiàn means to capture.

glosses.zh: 见全：得到保全，没有受害。
glosses.en: jiàn quán: was left whole, was spared.

glosses.zh: 使臣：朝廷派来收税的官员。
glosses.en: shǐ chén: envoys sent by the court, here to collect taxes.

glosses.zh: 将王命：带着皇帝的命令。将，拿着、带着。
glosses.en: jiāng wáng mìng: carrying the emperor's orders. Jiāng means to hold or carry.

glosses.zh: 岂不如贼焉：难道还比不上贼吗？
glosses.en: qǐ bù rú zéi yān: can they really be worse than the rebels?

glosses.zh: 征敛：收税，搜刮财物。
glosses.en: zhēng liǎn: to collect taxes, to squeeze money out of people.

glosses.zh: 迫之如火煎：逼百姓逼得像用火煎熬一样。
glosses.en: pò zhī rú huǒ jiān: they press the people as if frying them over a fire.

glosses.zh: 绝人命：断绝百姓的活路。
glosses.en: jué rén mìng: to cut off people's lives, to leave them no way to live.

glosses.zh: 时世贤：当时人眼里的好官、能干的官。
glosses.en: shí shì xián: what the times call a fine, able official.

glosses.zh: 委符节：交还官印，辞官不干了。委，丢下；符节，做官的凭证。
glosses.en: wěi fú jié: to give back the seal of office, to quit. Wěi means to put down; fú jié was the token that proved one's office.

glosses.zh: 引竿：拿起竹竿。
glosses.en: yǐn gān: to pick up a pole.

glosses.zh: 刺船：用竹竿撑船。
glosses.en: cì chuán: to push a boat along with a pole.

glosses.zh: 将家：带着家人。
glosses.en: jiāng jiā: taking the family along.

glosses.zh: 就鱼麦：到有鱼有麦的地方去，就是去过打鱼种田的生活。
glosses.en: jiù yú mài: to go where there are fish and wheat, that is, to live by fishing and farming.

glosses.zh: 归老：回去养老，度过晚年。
glosses.en: guī lǎo: to go home and grow old there.

translation.zh: 从前遇上天下太平的年月，
translation.en: In the old days, when the land was at peace,

translation.zh: 我在山林里住了二十来年。
translation.en: I lived among the hills and woods for some twenty years.

translation.zh: 泉水的源头就在院子门口，
translation.en: A spring rose right by my courtyard door,

translation.zh: 山洞和山谷正对着我的家门。
translation.en: and caves and valleys lay just outside my gate.

translation.zh: 交田税有固定的日子，
translation.en: Land tax was paid on fixed days,

translation.zh: 太阳升得老高还能安心睡觉。
translation.en: and we could sleep late without a care.

translation.zh: 忽然世道大乱，
translation.en: Then all at once the world fell into chaos,

translation.zh: 好几年我都亲身待在军营里。
translation.en: and for several years I lived in army camps.

translation.zh: 如今我来掌管这个州郡，
translation.en: Now I have come to govern this prefecture,

translation.zh: 山里的人又闹起乱来。
translation.en: and the hill people are rising up again.

translation.zh: 城太小，贼没有在这里屠杀，
translation.en: The town was so small the rebels did not slaughter it;

translation.zh: 百姓太穷，连贼都觉得可怜。
translation.en: the people were so poor that even the rebels felt pity.

translation.zh: 所以贼攻破了邻近的地方，
translation.en: So the rebels took the lands next door,

translation.zh: 只有这个州保全了下来。
translation.en: and only this prefecture was spared.

translation.zh: 朝廷派来的官员带着皇帝的命令，
translation.en: The envoys come bearing the emperor's orders,

translation.zh: 难道还比不上那些贼吗？
translation.en: so how can they be worse than the rebels?

translation.zh: 可现在那些来收税的人，
translation.en: Yet now those who come to collect taxes

translation.zh: 逼迫百姓就像用火煎熬。
translation.en: press the people as if frying them over a fire.

translation.zh: 谁能狠心断绝百姓的活路，
translation.en: Who could bear to cut off the people's lives

translation.zh: 去换一个当世好官的名声？
translation.en: just to be praised as a fine official of the day?

translation.zh: 我想交还官印辞去官职，
translation.en: I would rather give back my seal of office,

translation.zh: 拿起竹竿自己撑着小船，
translation.en: take up a pole and push my own boat,

translation.zh: 带着家人去有鱼有麦的地方，
translation.en: and take my family where there are fish and wheat,

translation.zh: 在江湖边上安度晚年。
translation.en: to grow old by the rivers and lakes.

background.zh: 唐代宗广德元年（763年，癸卯年），西原一带的人起兵作乱，攻进道州（今湖南道县），烧杀抢掠。第二年元结来做道州刺史。这一年乱兵又攻打永州、邵州，却没有侵犯道州就退走了。元结认为这不是道州有力量打败他们，而是乱兵可怜这里的百姓太穷。可朝廷派来的官员还在拼命逼百姓交税。他就写了这首诗给官吏们看。
background.en: In 763, people from the Xiyuan area in the far south rose up and broke into Daozhou (today's Dao County in Hunan). They burned, killed and robbed. The next year Yuan Jie came to govern Daozhou. That year the rebels attacked Yongzhou and Shaozhou nearby, but left Daozhou alone and went away. Yuan Jie believed this was not because Daozhou was strong. It was because the rebels pitied how poor the people were. Yet the envoys sent by the court were still forcing the people to pay heavy taxes. So he wrote this poem to show the officials.

author_note.zh: 元结（719—772），唐代诗人，也做过官，带过兵。他写诗喜欢说真话，关心百姓的苦难。在道州做刺史时，他写了《舂陵行》和这首诗，都替穷苦百姓说话。杜甫读了很感动，专门写诗称赞他。
author_note.en: Yuan Jie (719–772) was a Tang poet who also served as an official and led troops. He liked to write plain truths in his poems and cared about the suffering of ordinary people. While governing Daozhou he wrote "The Song of Chongling" and this poem, both speaking up for the poor. Du Fu was moved when he read them and wrote a poem in praise of him.

appreciation.zh: 这首诗像一篇讲道理的信。开头先回忆太平年月：家门口有泉水山谷，交税有规矩，人能睡个安稳觉。接着写战乱，写道州的穷。最扎心的是中间一层对比：乱兵都可怜百姓，放过了道州；朝廷派来的官员却像火煎一样逼人交税。诗人反问：难道官还不如贼吗？最后他说，宁可丢掉官职去打鱼种田，也不愿踩着百姓的命去当“好官”。语言朴素，没有华丽的词，却句句有力，能看出一个好官的良心。
appreciation.en: This poem reads like a letter that argues a point. It opens with memories of peaceful days: a spring and valleys by the door, taxes collected by the rules, and nights of easy sleep. Then it turns to the war and to how poor Daozhou is. The sharpest part is a contrast in the middle. The rebels pitied the people and spared the town, but the court's envoys squeeze out taxes as if frying people over a fire. The poet asks: can officials really be worse than rebels? At the end he says he would rather quit and go fishing and farming than become a "fine official" by trampling on people's lives. The words are plain, with nothing fancy, yet every line is strong. You can see the conscience of a good official.
